Memory-and-Data-Model.title: Memory and data model
Memory-and-Data-Model.classification: Current evidence-first direction; canonical memory placement unresolved
Memory-and-Data-Model.summary: Separates structured run evidence, HIMS records, configuration, artifacts, and future canonical memory rather than calling every stored file Huey's memory.
Memory-and-Data-Model.body:
## Current useful data classes

| Class | Purpose |
|---|---|
| **Run record** | Identifies one V1 or integration execution and its stages |
| **Input artifact** | Known media, checksum, provenance, and preparation details |
| **Transcript** | Local transcription output and fidelity assessment |
| **Response artifact** | Provider request/response metadata with secrets excluded |
| **Event** | Attributable state transition, decision, warning, or failure |
| **Configuration snapshot** | Relevant non-secret configuration and versions |
| **Hardware profile** | Exact device, revision, firmware, battery, and observed state |
| **Controller identity** | Provisioned device identity, status, and revocation history |
| **Release manifest** | Files, checksums, versions, provenance, and validation |

## Current boundary

Structured logs and HIMS ledger/storage work exist. The exact location, schema, retention, signing, and authority of canonical Huey memory remain unresolved. A convenient SQLite table or copied archive must not be promoted to canonical memory merely because it exists.

## Historical schema warning

The 2025 `Memory-Schema-v2` wiki page is lineage, not an accepted current schema. Useful ideas such as immutable events, artifact hashes, and snapshots may be retained only through explicit current design and migration work.
